value: moi is a disjunctive pronoun
affirmative counterpart : moi aussi

evidence.notes: Usage note states moi aussi is used after an affirmative statement; source example 'Elle n'aime pas le bruit. Moi non plus.' Confidence high.

value: passé composé with être : ils sont montés en haut de la Tour Eiffel
equivalent : monter au sommet de

evidence.notes: Source example 'Ils sont montés en haut de la Tour Eiffel' shows the être auxiliary; monter au sommet de is the listed alias. Confidence high.

value: transitive use takes avoir : ils ont monté les malles
à + place : monter les malles au grenier

evidence.notes: Source example 'Ils ont monté les malles au grenier' shows the avoir auxiliary and the à complement. Confidence high.

value: ne + importe is fixed, with elision n' before importe
as an exclamation it means nonsense or something absurd

evidence.notes: Usage note states the exclamatory use means nonsense; the form always elides to n'importe. Confidence high.

value: negated form normally takes the subjunctive
indicative possible when the speaker treats the proposition as factual

evidence.notes: Listed restriction states the subjunctive is optional and marks more uncertainty; source example 'Je ne crois pas que Daniel soit coupable'. Confidence high.

value: negated form normally takes the subjunctive
indicative possible when the speaker treats the proposition as factual

evidence.notes: Listed restriction states the subjunctive is optional and marks more uncertainty; usage note states the negation places the proposition in doubt. Confidence high.

value: ne becomes n' before a vowel
jamais follows the auxiliary in the passé composé : je n'ai jamais vu

evidence.notes: Standard negation pattern; jamais occupies the position between auxiliary and past participle. Confidence high.

value: formal register
ne becomes n' before a vowel : ce n'est guère raisonnable

evidence.notes: Listed restriction states formal register; source example 'Ce n'est guère raisonnable' shows the elision. Confidence high.

value: ne becomes n' before a vowel

value: ne becomes n' before a vowel or mute h
